items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Tad didn't offer Miles enough money, so Miles wouldn't accept a job, but he came and played with us every night.

ctx.x: just put it , because as soon as we finished playing I would walk outside because I was afraid the band was going to be busted. It was freezing outside.

But the man would come to work with us, I mean the man who sold the dope, he came to work. It was a regular job with him, he came and sat right beside the band and so he furnished the band with dope, you know. But a great band. But at this time -- let's see, I'll tell you. Miles, who at that time -- I don't think Miles even drank beer. Miles -- Tad didn't offer Miles enough money, so Miles wouldn't accept a job, but he came and played with us every night. But this is the truth. Tad was paying the band out of his…

So most of the guys -- he had to pay out of his pocket, because this was above scale, but he couldn't pay Miles enough so Miles would just come in and play any way, but he wouldn't accept the money. So wait a minute. Tad paid me, gave me a check one night for my salary, and it so happened that my wife worked at the bank that he wrote this check on, and I knew what he had in the bank. I think he had about $12.00 in his account, and he gave me a check at this time for $125.00, which was a lot of money then. And I…
